clue.text: One cracking secure phone?

parts.note: secure means safe, out of danger
blower is British slang for a telephone

explanation.surface: Someone breaking into a telephone line that is supposed to be protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' suggests breaking a code on a phone; here it is the criminal who cracks open strongboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal who blasts open strongboxes is one who does the cracking, in the burglar's sense.

clue.text: What's wedged in strings of the piano?

indicators.note: what's wedged in points to letters lying inside a run of clue words

explanation.surface: A question about what is jammed between the strings of a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' in music means quietly, so it defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction to play quietly, which means gently or quietly.

clue.text: Rush one out of freezing cold, wrapped in woolly stuff?

parts.note: to rush away is to flee

indicators.note: out of says one letter leaves the word for freezing cold

parts.note: iced means freezing cold
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying out of the bitter cold, bundled up in wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes I from ICED, leaving CED. The definition is cryptic: covered in fleece; the usual sense is swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally covered in a fleece, the woolly coat of a sheep, while the usual meaning is swindled.

clue.text: One should have gone before living on this

definitions.text: One should have gone before living on this

parts.words: One should have gone before living on this
parts.note: someone who ought already to have died is surviving beyond their expected span

explanation.surface: A grim remark about someone who has outstayed their welcome in life.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'living on' it means surviving past the point when death or failure was expected.

clue.text: Wrong to support a single playwright

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the wrong word comes last

parts.note: one means a single
ill means wrong, as in ill-advised

explanation.surface: A dramatist who backs a single wrong cause.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'to support' puts ILL beneath ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was an American dramatist, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: January date? Happen one falls out with start of year

indicators.note: falls out suggests a quarrel or disarray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: start of takes only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A January day on which something happens to start the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls out' rearranges HAPPEN plus I; 'start of' adds Y from year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the Magi's visit falls on 6 January, Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Put up picture — a new look, without frame?

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its first and last letters, which are dropped here

parts.note: a change is a new look, a fresh appearance

explanation.surface: Redecorating a room: hang the painting, perhaps without its frame for a fresh look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without frame' removes the first and last letters, C and E, from CHANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a picture up on the wall is to hang it, the gallery verb for displaying artwork.

clue.text: A short time's great on the run

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, a time shortened
large means great in size

explanation.surface: A quick moment of greatness for someone running.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped criminal still free is said to be loose, which is what on the run means.

clue.text: Some absorbed by recycling energy?

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside, so the word for some goes into the rearranged letters
recycling means processing again into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: A physics question about energy taken up by a reprocessing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' rearranges the letters into GREENY; the whole clue also describes the environmentalist party.
explanation.definitionFit: The environmentalist political party includes members devoted to recycling and renewable energy.

clue.text: The flower of France, disfigured in rifle duels

indicators.note: something disfigured has its shape spoiled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gallant Frenchmen damaged in duels fought with rifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disfigured' rearranges RIFLE DUELS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The stylised lily is the traditional heraldic emblem of the French monarchy, literally 'lily flower'.

clue.text: Run line that's brought in payment

indicators.note: brought in says the line's letter is put inside the payment word

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: A railway line has been introduced in exchange for a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger is to flee, a direct synonym.

clue.text: It's a good habit you'll get into, using this

definitions.text: It's a good habit you'll get into, using this

parts.words: It's a good habit you'll get into, using this
parts.note: habit here is clothing, as a monk's habit, and the tool smartens a garment before you put it on

explanation.surface: Advice that a useful routine will develop if you use a certain tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush for removing lint from garments keeps the clothes, or habit, tidy.

clue.text: They may be classed among the crocodiles

definitions.text: They may be classed among the crocodiles

parts.words: They may be classed among the crocodiles
parts.note: a crocodile in Britain is a line of pupils walking in pairs, and 'classed' hints at school classes rather than zoological classification

explanation.surface: A zoologist's remark about which animals count as crocodilians.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a crocodile is a line of children walking two by two, as on a school outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils walking in a paired line on an outing make up a crocodile, and they are also in classes.

clue.text: It keeps the nippers away from sensitive pets

definitions.text: It keeps the nippers away from sensitive pets

parts.words: It keeps the nippers away from sensitive pets
parts.note: nippers sounds like small children, but here the biting insects that plague cats and dogs

explanation.surface: Something that stops children bothering nervous pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nippers' is British slang for small children; here it is biting insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A neckband treated with insecticide keeps parasites off cats and dogs.

clue.text: Totter after long run

indicators.note: after puts the totter word behind the long letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for long, as on clothing sizes
a totter is one who tots up, an adder of figures

explanation.surface: Someone staggering at the end of a long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totter' looks like a verb for staggering; read it as one who tots up figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in tights or stockings is called a ladder in British English.

clue.text: One hated article by those people in motoring group

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places the article and pronoun inside the motoring group's letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A loathed piece written about some people in a car club.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA (Automobile Association) is a British breakdown and motoring club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or loathed is described as an object of utter detestation, a person or thing hated.

clue.text: Having a lookout, perhaps, for English painter

parts.note: to land something is to get it, so having it
a seer is one who sees, as a lookout does

explanation.surface: An English artist who keeps watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter, known for animal pictures and the Trafalgar Square lions.

clue.text: Dog the French repelled — one possessed by the devil

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the French article is read backwards

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)

indicators.note: possessed by puts one inside the devil, as if he holds it

parts.note: Satan is the devil
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dog that the French drove away, a creature possessed by Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns LA into AL; 'possessed by' places I in SATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is the British name for the German shepherd dog.

clue.text: What sounds like minor distraction?

indicators.note: these words say the next word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: slight means minor or small

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as a small diversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a conjuror's trickery that relies on drawing attention away.

clue.text: Allow a comment from the hairdresser?

definitions.meaning: to give leave or authorise something
a stylist might say '...', suggesting a permanent wave for the hair

explanation.surface: Giving permission, perhaps from a salon stylist.
explanation.definitionFit: To give consent is to let something happen, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One hopes my deliveries will be bouncers

definitions.text: One hopes my deliveries will be bouncers

parts.words: One hopes my deliveries will be bouncers
parts.note: deliveries and bouncers sound like cricket bowling, but here are newborn babies who are bonny and healthy

explanation.surface: A fast bowler hoping to bowl short-pitched balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a ball that rears up at the batsman; here it is a bouncing baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who assists at childbirth delivers babies and hopes they are healthy and bouncing.

clue.text: Sent up a cry for help, swallowing mother's exotic snack

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the letters read from bottom to top
swallowing puts the mother word inside the call for help

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Someone signals for help after a parent's foreign snack goes down badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' in a down clue turns the whole run, giving A SOMAS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried pastry triangle filled with spiced vegetables or meat is a South Asian snack.

clue.text: You won't put my coffin lid anywhere else!

definitions.text: You won't put my coffin lid anywhere else!

parts.words: You won't put my coffin lid anywhere else!
parts.note: the lid can only be placed on top of the deceased's corpse, playing literally on the phrase of defiant refusal

explanation.surface: Someone fiercely insisting on how their own coffin is to be closed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses absolute refusal, literally meaning only once I am dead and buried.

clue.text: Eager to promote new joint

indicators.note: to promote means to move something higher, so the letter for new rises up the word

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: Keen to advance a fresh joint venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' moves N from the end of KEEN up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg's hinged middle articulation is a joint, the one between thigh and shin.

clue.text: Love girls' extremities — ie, these?

indicators.note: extremities are the ends, so take the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: An admirer confesses a fondness for the limbs of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremities' takes the first and last letters of Love and girls': L, E, G, S; the whole clue then defines limbs as extremities.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbs are the body's extremities, and the clue asks whether these are what it means.

clue.text: Clarifying decision

definitions.meaning: making clear, as a problem is cleared up or settled
a firm determination or formal vote made by a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both the clearing up of a difficulty and a firm decision such as a New Year's pledge.

clue.text: Girl, in fact, taking time off

indicators.note: taking with off signals removing the time letter from the word
off completes the instruction to remove the time letter

parts.note: fact means truth, so 'in fact' is 'in truth'

explanation.surface: A girl who, really, is taking a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's name, a biblical one.

clue.text: Unfinished Test allowed to occupy the versatile sporting type

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for test is dropped

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: to occupy places allowed inside the following word

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: An incomplete cricket Test, with an all-rounder allowed to take part.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, which makes the surface look like a sports report.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in swimming, cycling and running events is a versatile all-round sporting type.
